newsitem.title: GERMANY: German to send aid, but no troops to Zaire.
newsitem.headline: German to send aid, but no troops to Zaire.

text.p: Germany said on Thursday it will step up its contributions in humanitarian aid to Zaire but has no plans to send troops to a multinational force being assembled to protect aid routes into the country.
A government spokesman said Germany had send equipment and aid worth 354 million marks ($235 million) to Zaire since 1994.
It had also contributed an emergency 2.4 million mark payment at the end of October and plans to make 5.2 million marks available for water purification facilities.
"Germany does not intend to have soldiers of the Bundeswehr participating in the force being assembled," the spokesman said.
The decision was criticised by the foreign policy spokesman of the opposition Social Democrats (SPD), Guenter Verheugen.
"It is wrong to reject the possibility of participation from the outset without even knowing the details of the international mission," he told a German radio station. ($1=1.5061 Mark)
